title: Gameweek 4 Hall of Shame: the blanks, the cameos, and the captain who cost you
dek: The awards nobody wants from Gameweek 4, starting with B.Fernandes. Every one of them a real number, which is the problem.
body:
## The awards nobody wants

Every gameweek produces a handful of moments that are only funny once they cannot hurt you any more. Gameweek 4 has finished, so here they are.

Every award below is a real lookup against the round's data. Nothing here is invented, which is the part that stings.

:::takeaways
- **B.Fernandes** takes the Golden Blank at £12.0m.
- The field captained **Haaland** for 9 points.
- **Bogle** scored 15 at 3% ownership.
:::

###  The Golden Blank

£12.0m buys a lot of things. On this occasion it bought 90 minutes of **B.Fernandes** and 2 points, which 41.7% of you had budgeted for rather differently.

###  The Armband Tax

**Haaland** was the popular armband and returned 9 points, which the armband turned into 18. A rare week where the crowd and the scoreboard agreed.

###  The One You Did Not Own

15 points from **Bogle**, owned by 3%. Somewhere a very small number of people are having their best Saturday of the season and telling absolutely everybody.

###  Cameo of the Week

15 minutes. 7 points. **Igor Jesus** did more after coming on than several people did all afternoon, most of them in your starting eleven.

###  Best Value on the Board

**Davis**, £4.0m, 14 points, 3.5 per million. Quietly the most sensible thing that happened all weekend.

###  Mugged by the Woodwork

**E.Le Fée** generated 1.44 expected goal involvements and converted precisely none of them. The underlying numbers liked him a great deal more than the scoreboard did, which is either a buy signal or a warning depending on how your season is going.

## For the record

The average manager scored **69**, the best score in the game was **151**, and the gap between them was 82 points — roughly a captain, a bench and a small amount of luck.

:::callout insight
None of this is advice. The advice is next door, and it is considerably better behaved.
:::
